newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia coastguards kill Turkish fisherman.
newsitem.headline: Russia coastguards kill Turkish fisherman.

text.p: A Turkish fisherman, injured when Russian coastguards fired on a boat caught fishing in Georgia's Black Sea territorial waters, died in hospital on Wednesday, Russian RIA news agency said.

Russian coastguard cutters, which patrol the area under an agreement with the Georgian government, were sent early Wednesday to intercept nine Turkish vessels spotted in the former Soviet republic's territorial waters.
A Russian border guard spokesman said later that all the boats fled except one, which, the spokesman said, began to execute what he called a dangerous manoeuvre.
"The coastguard boat fired warning shots ordering the Turkish vessel to stop," he said. "The poachers did not respond and the guards shot at the vessel."
The spokesman said one fisherman was badly injured. He and the damaged boat were taken to the Georgian port of Batumi, which is the base for the Russian coastguards.
RIA quoted Georgian chief boderguard Valery Chkheidze as saying that the fisherman later died in hospital. He gave no further details.
Russia has complained that violations by Turkish fishing boats have become frequent in recent months. Turkey, Russian officials say, acknowledges the infringements but can do little to stop them.
